newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Opposition MP now an independent.
newsitem.headline: Opposition MP now an independent.

text.p: Vincent Lasse, a member of Parliament, declared himself an independent on Wednesday, breaking ranks with the Opposition People's National Movement party.
Lasse, MP for the southwestern Trinidad district of Point Fortin, said in a message faxed to radio and television stations he could not work with the leadership of the party led by Patrick Manning.
He was housing minister from 1991 to 1995.
Lasse's resignation reduced the strength of the Opposition People's National Movement party (PNM) in the House of Representatives to 16 from 17.
Neither Manning nor party chairman Linda Baboolal could be reached for comment. But deputy political leader Kenneth Valley told Reuters he was unaware of the development.
After the PNM lost power following the Nov 5, 1995, general elections, there has been mounting criticism against its leadership and calls for his resignation.
Members of the party's hierarchy said they objected to Manning's decision to call elections 13 months ahead of schedule.
In his faxed message, Lasse said he quit the party in the interest of national unity and he had no regrets.
Manning, opposition leader in parliament, was last year re- elected political leader of the 40-year-old PNM.
On Friday the Electoral College comprising members of the House of Representatives and the Senate will elect a new president to succeed Noor Hassanali who is retiring.
